legend: Pulmonary diffuse large B-cell lymphoma consisting of medium-sized to large atypical lymphoid cells with a high N:C ratio, mildly irregular nuclear contours, fine even chromatin, and inconspicuous nucleoli, from an endobronchial ultrasound–guided transbronchial FNAB of a lower lobe lung mass (liquid-based preparation, Pap).

Pulmonary diffuse large B-cell lymphoma consisting of atypical medium-sized to large atypical lymphoid cells (note the comparison with a bronchial epithelial cell in the upper-right corner), from an endobronchial ultrasound–guided transbronchial FNAB of a large right lower lobe lung mass. Immunostaining showed the atypical lymphoid cells to be positive for CD20, with a Ki-67 proliferation index of approximately 80% (not shown) (liquid-based preparation, Pap).

Chronic cough, persistent infiltrates, and atelectasis in the right upper lobe. Concomitant histology: MALT lymphoma in the right upper lobe. Cellular smear with numerous lymphoid cells of varying size. Only a few respiratory epithelial cells are present (bronchial brushing, H&E).

Chronic cough, persistent infiltrates, and atelectasis in the right upper lobe. Concomitant histology: MALT lymphoma in the right upper lobe. Cellular smear with numerous lymphoid cells of varying size. Many cytoplasmic fragments in the background, with one ciliated respiratory epithelial cell (bronchial brushing, H&E).

Chronic cough, persistent infiltrates, and atelectasis in the right upper lobe. Concomitant histology: MALT lymphoma in the right upper lobe. Numerous lymphoid cells of varying size. In the centre there is a blastic cell with a large nucleolus. Many degenerated nuclei are present and there are many cytoplasmic fragments in the background (bronchial brushing, Giemsa).
